subject: Biology
examFormat: Three papers, all compulsory; Papers 1 and 2 are taken as a composite paper at one sitting. Paper 1: 50 multiple-choice questions from Section A, 50 marks, 50 minutes. Paper 2: essay paper of 70 marks lasting 1 hour 40 minutes; candidates answer two of four Section A questions (20 marks each) and the compulsory short-structured questions from Section C (30 marks) for Nigeria. Paper 3: practical test of 2 hours and 80 marks; two compulsory Section A questions (25 marks each) and one Section C question (30 marks) for Nigeria.
excluded: Section B (for candidates in Ghana only) was left out; it covers Introducing Biology, Cell Biology, Life Processes in Living Things, Diversity of Living Things, Interactions in Nature, Mammalian Anatomy and Physiology, Plant Structure and Physiology, Humans and their Environment, Evolution and Biology and Industry.

topics.name: Classification of Living Things
topics.content: Kingdom Monera (Prokaryotes): single-celled, motile or non-motile organisms without definite nucleus e.g. bacteria and blue-green algae. Kingdom Protista (Eukaryotes): single-celled, motile or non-motile organisms with complex cell structure and definite nucleus e.g. Chlamydomonas, Amoeba. Major phyla of Kingdom Protoctista include Rhizopoda, Zoomastigina, Apicomplexa, Ciliophora, Euglenophyta, Oomycota, Chlorophyta, Rhodophyta and Phaeophyta. Kingdom Fungi (Eukaryotes): mainly non-motile organisms composed of hyphae containing nuclei e.g. moulds, mushrooms and Rhizopus; major phyla include Zygomycota, Ascomycota and Basidiomycota. Kingdom Plantae (Eukaryotes): mainly multicellular non-motile organisms containing chlorophyll that enables them to photosynthesize e.g. mosses, ferns, pines, oil palms and yam plants; divisions and classes include Bryophyta (Hepaticae, Musci), Lycopodophyta, Filicinophyta, Coniferophyta, Cycadophyta and Angiospermophyta (Monocotyledoneae and Dicotyledoneae). Kingdom Animalia (Eukaryotes): multicellular motile organisms that feed on other organisms e.g. corals, worms, insects, snails, fishes, frogs, snakes, monkeys, cows. Viruses should be mentioned as a link between living and non-living things.

subtopics.name: Living and non-living things
objectives: Classify objects into living and non-living, giving examples of each group
State that viruses are a link between living and non-living things

subtopics.name: Classification into Kingdoms
objectives: Classify living things into the Kingdoms Monera, Protoctista (Protista), Fungi, Plantae and Animalia
Describe the major characteristics of the major phyla of Kingdoms Protoctista and Fungi
Describe the characteristics of the major divisions and classes of Kingdom Plantae
Describe the characteristics of the major phyla and classes of Kingdom Animalia
Describe the external features of the cockroach, butterfly, Tilapia, toad/frog, lizard and domestic fowl/pigeon

subtopics.name: Differences between plants and animals
objectives: Distinguish between plants and animals

topics.name: Organization of Life
topics.content: Levels of organization: (i) cell (single-celled organisms): Amoeba, Euglena, Paramecium; (ii) tissue: Hydra; (iii) organ (storage organ): bulb, rhizome and heart; (iv) system/organ system in mammals and flowering plants e.g. reproductive system, excretory system. The examples should be used to illustrate differentiation and specialization in organisms. The significance of different levels of organization, including volume/surface area ratio, should be mentioned.

subtopics.name: Levels of organization
objectives: Describe the cell, tissue, organ and organ system levels of organization with examples
Use examples to illustrate differentiation and specialization in organisms

subtopics.name: Complexity of organization in higher organisms
objectives: State the advantages and disadvantages of complexity of organization in higher organisms
Explain the significance of different levels of organization, including volume/surface area ratio

topics.name: Forms in which Living Cells Exist
objectives: Describe single and free-living cells: Amoeba, Paramecium, Euglena and Chlamydomonas
Describe a colony (Volvox) and a filament (Spirogyra)
Identify cells that are part of a living organism: cheek cells, onion root tip cells and epidermis of fleshy leaves
Distinguish groups of cells that form tissues from those that form colonies or filaments
Relate the structure of these organisms to their forms of existence to illustrate dependence and interdependence

topics.name: Cell Structure and Functions
objectives: Describe the structure of the cell: cell wall, cell membrane, nucleus, cytoplasm and cytoplasmic organelles
State the functions of mitochondria, lysosomes, chloroplasts, endoplasmic reticulum, ribosomes, centrosomes, Golgi bodies and chromosomes
State the similarities and differences between plant and animal cells

topics.name: The Cell and its Environment
objectives: Explain diffusion, osmosis and active transport as physical and biophysical processes
Explain the significance of these processes as factors that affect cell activities in the cell's environment
Mention haemolysis, plasmolysis, turgidity and crenation

topics.name: Properties and Functions of the Living Cell

subtopics.name: Nutrition in the cell
objectives: Describe autotrophic nutrition (photosynthesis), with nutrition in Euglena, Chlamydomonas and Spirogyra
Describe heterotrophic (holozoic) nutrition, with nutrition in Amoeba and Paramecium

subtopics.name: Cellular respiration
objectives: Define and describe aerobic respiration, anaerobic respiration and energy release
Outline the chemical processes involved in glycolysis and Kreb's cycle, with reference to the role of ATP
State the importance of anaerobic respiration in food processing

subtopics.name: Excretion in single-celled organisms
objectives: Describe excretion in single-celled aquatic organisms by diffusion across the body surface and by contractile vacuole
Name the waste products of metabolism, with reference to carbon dioxide, water and ammonia

subtopics.name: Growth
objectives: Explain the basis of growth: cell division (mitosis), enlargement and differentiation
Describe the aspects of growth: increase in dry weight, irreversible increase in size and length, and increase in number of cells
Identify the regions of fastest growth in plants by observing root tip and shoot tip
Explain the influence of growth hormones and auxins on growth
Demonstrate growth curvatures (tropisms)

subtopics.name: Development in the cell
objectives: Describe development as enlargement and differentiation
Examine microscopically the regions of cell division, elongation, differentiation and maturation
Describe the processes that result in primary and secondary growth

subtopics.name: Movement in the cell
objectives: Describe organelles for movement: cilia and flagella
Describe cyclosis

subtopics.name: Types of reproduction
objectives: Describe asexual reproduction: fission, budding and vegetative propagation
Describe sexual reproduction: conjugation, gametogenesis and fertilization
Observe and draw prepared slides of fission in Paramecium, budding in yeast and Chlamydomonas, and conjugation in Paramecium and Spirogyra
Mention the process of meiosis

topics.name: Tissues and Supporting Systems
topics.content: Candidates should be familiar with the general plan of the mammalian skeleton and the different types of joints, and be able to identify, draw, label and state the functions of the individual bones listed in the content column. Detailed structure of the skull and histological structure of bones and cartilages will not be required. The relationship of skeleton and muscles during movement should be used to illustrate the different functions of the skeleton. In plants, turgid parenchyma, collenchyma, xylem (wood) and sclerenchyma should be studied; candidates should cut and draw the low power T.S. of stem and root of a herbaceous plant and label the epidermis, cortex and stele.

subtopics.name: Skeleton and supporting systems in animals
objectives: State the biological significance of skeleton and supporting systems
Name skeletal materials: bone, cartilage and chitin
Describe the types of skeleton: exoskeleton, endoskeleton and hydrostatic skeleton
Identify the bones of the vertebral column, girdles and long bones of the appendicular skeleton
Explain the mechanism of support in animals
State and explain the functions of the skeleton: protection, support, locomotion and respiratory movement

subtopics.name: Supporting tissues in plants
objectives: Describe the different types of supporting tissues in plants and their main features
State the functions of supporting tissues in plants: strength, rigidity (resistance against wind and water), flexibility and resilience

topics.name: Transport System
objectives: Explain the need for transport: surface area/volume ratio and movement of substances over greater distances
Name the media of transport: cytoplasm in cells, cell sap or latex in most plants and body fluid in invertebrates
topics.content: Source of materials, the forms in which they are transported and where they are transported to should be studied. Candidates should be familiar with the general circulatory system and open circulatory systems in invertebrates. Names of blood vessels responsible for transporting excretory products, gases, digested food and other nutrients should be mentioned.

subtopics.name: Transport in animals
objectives: Describe the structure of the heart, arteries, veins and capillaries
Describe the composition and function of blood and lymph
Describe the transport of excretory products, gases, digested food and other nutrients

subtopics.name: Uptake and movement of water and mineral salts in plants
objectives: Describe the uptake of water and mineral salts from the soil into a plant and their movement through the plant
Carry out experiments using eosin solution to show water and mineral salts uptake

subtopics.name: Translocation
objectives: Describe the movement of organic materials from leaves to roots
Explain the basic theories underlying translocation: pressure flow hypothesis and cytoplasmic streaming
Perform the ringing experiment to show that synthesized organic nutrients are transported through the phloem

subtopics.name: Transpiration
objectives: State the advantages and disadvantages of transpiration
Describe the types of transpiration and the environmental factors affecting transpiration
Determine the rate of transpiration by experiment

subtopics.name: Movement of water to the apex of trees and herbs
objectives: Explain the physiological factors affecting the rise of water in the xylem: root pressure, transpiration, cohesion-tension mechanism, adhesion and water potential gradient

topics.name: Respiratory System
objectives: Describe respiration through the body surface: cutaneous, gills and lungs
Describe the characteristics of respiratory surfaces
Mention the respiratory organs of insects
Observe, draw and label the respiratory organs of a bony fish (e.g. Tilapia) and a small mammal (e.g. rat)
Describe the mechanisms of gaseous exchange in fish, toad, mammals and plants
Describe respiratory movements in these animals and the mechanisms of opening and closing of stomata

topics.name: Excretory Systems and Mechanisms
objectives: Describe the types of excretory systems: kidney, stomata and lenticels
Describe the characteristics of excretory organs in these systems
Observe, draw and label the excretory organs of a small mammal (e.g. rat)
Explain the concept of excretion in plants
Mention the excretory products of plants: water, carbon dioxide, oxygen, alkaloids, tannins, gums, resins and acids

subtopics.name: Kidney: structure and functions
objectives: Describe the structure and functions of the kidney
Mention osmoregulation, excretion and maintenance of acid-base balance
Mention conditions that affect kidney function such as water and salt content of the blood and environmental temperature
Mention excretory products such as urea, water, salts and uric acid

subtopics.name: Liver
objectives: State the functions of the liver
Identify the liver and its position relative to the gall bladder, bile duct, pancreas, duodenum and stomach

subtopics.name: Skin (homeostasis)
objectives: Describe the structure and function of the skin
Observe, draw and label the mammalian skin
Explain the regulation of the internal environment by the skin

subtopics.name: Animal hormones
objectives: State the site of secretion, functions and effects of over- and under-secretion of hormones
Mention the endocrine glands (pituitary, thyroid, adrenal, pancreas, gonads) and their secretions
Describe the stages in the metamorphosis of the toad and the role of thyroxine

subtopics.name: Plant hormones
objectives: Mention the effects of auxins on lateral bud development, leaf fall and initiation of adventitious roots
Make reference to crop harvesting, growth and weed control

subtopics.name: The central nervous system
objectives: Name the components of the central nervous system
Describe the parts of the brain and their functions: cerebrum, cerebellum, medulla oblongata and hypothalamus
Describe the structure and function of the spinal cord
Locate the brain and spinal cord in a dissected vertebrate and identify the regions of the brain

subtopics.name: Peripheral nervous system
objectives: Describe the somatic nervous system
Describe the autonomic nervous system (functions of the sympathetic and parasympathetic systems only)
Describe the structure and functions of the neurone and observe, draw and label a neurone from a slide
Classify neurones: afferent (sensory), efferent (motor) and intermediate

subtopics.name: Types of nervous actions
objectives: Describe the reflex arc
Distinguish reflex and voluntary actions and state the differences between them
Perform experiments to illustrate reflex actions such as blinking, knee jerk and withdrawal of hand from hot objects
Describe conditioned reflex and its role in behaviour, enumerating examples such as salivation, driving a car, walking and swimming

topics.name: Sense Organs
topics.content: Candidates should examine the mammalian eye noting the shape, colour and positions of the optic muscle and optic nerve. Mention should be made of eye defects and their corrections.

subtopics.name: Eye
objectives: Describe the structure and function of the eye
Mention eye defects and their corrections

subtopics.name: Ear
objectives: Describe the structure and function of the ear

subtopics.name: Reproductive system of mammals
objectives: Describe the structure and function of male and female reproductive systems
State the differences between male and female reproductive organs
Describe the structure of the gametes (sperm and ovum)
Describe fertilization, development of the embryo and birth
Explain the different methods of birth control

subtopics.name: Metamorphosis in insects
objectives: Describe metamorphosis in insects using the life histories of butterfly and cockroach to illustrate complete and incomplete metamorphosis
Draw and label the stages in the life history of butterfly and cockroach

subtopics.name: Comparison of reproduction in vertebrates
objectives: Compare reproduction in fish, amphibian, reptile, bird and mammal with reference to method of fertilization, number of eggs and parental care

subtopics.name: Floral parts
objectives: Describe the arrangement of floral parts of a named insect-pollinated and a named wind-pollinated flower
Describe the structure and function of the male and female parts of a flower

subtopics.name: Pollination in plants
objectives: Describe the types of pollination, with named examples
State the features of cross-pollinated and self-pollinated flowers and relate flower features to agents of pollination
Name the agents of pollination
Describe the kinds of placentation: axile, marginal and parietal

subtopics.name: Development of the zygote in flowering plants
objectives: Describe fertilization and the process of development of the zygote in flowering plants
Observe germinated pollen grains in sucrose solution and slides or charts of stages of embryo development

subtopics.name: Fruits
objectives: Classify fruits (types of fruits) into dry and fleshy fruits
Describe the structure of fruits, examining and drawing the internal structure of a leguminous fruit, orange, maize and tomato

subtopics.name: Dispersal of fruits and seeds
objectives: Describe the agents of dispersal of fruits and seeds
Study the features aiding dispersal in sunflower (achene), Combretum, cotton, Crotalaria/bean, Desmodium, Bidens sp., Tridax sp. and coconut
Distinguish between a fruit and a seed

topics.name: Plant Nutrition
topics.content: Photosynthesis: biochemical nature, photoactivation of chlorophyll resulting in conversion of light energy to ATP and reduction of NADP (biochemical detail is not required).

subtopics.name: Photosynthesis
objectives: Describe the process of photosynthesis and its chemical equation
Describe the light and dark reactions
State the materials and conditions necessary for photosynthesis
Give evidence of photosynthesis, including testing for starch in green leaves
Mention the fate of the products of photosynthesis, and the translocation and storage of excess food

subtopics.name: Mineral requirement of plants
objectives: Describe mineral nutrition: macro and micro-nutrients
Name the macro elements (carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen, potassium, phosphorus, magnesium, sulphur, calcium, iron) and micro elements (copper, manganese, zinc, boron)
Describe the soil and atmosphere as sources of mineral elements
Distinguish between food produced and mineral elements

topics.name: Animal Nutrition
topics.content: Local examples as sources of food substances should be given, with reference to the food relationship between plants and animals.

subtopics.name: Food substances
objectives: Name the classes and sources of food substances
Relate food substances to local examples

subtopics.name: Balanced diet
objectives: Describe a balanced diet and its importance, stressing the importance of each class of food
Relate the idea of balanced diet to one's own diet
Mention malnutrition and its effects on humans

subtopics.name: Food tests
objectives: Carry out tests for starch, reducing sugar, protein, fats and oil
Perform experiments to show that ptyalin in saliva changes cooked starch to reducing sugar

subtopics.name: Digestive enzymes
objectives: State the classes, characteristics and functions of digestive enzymes
State the source, site of action, substrate and effect of each digestive enzyme
Carry out experiments on the characteristics of enzymes, including effects of pH, temperature and concentration

subtopics.name: Modes of nutrition
objectives: Describe autotrophic nutrition (photosynthesis)
Describe heterotrophic nutrition: holozoic, parasitic, symbiotic and saprophytic, using named examples

subtopics.name: Alimentary system
objectives: Describe the alimentary tract of different animals, comparing a dissected named bird and mammal
Describe the parts of the alimentary canal, their functions and modifications reflecting digestive function

subtopics.name: Dental formula
objectives: Explain the meaning of dental formula and determine the dental formulae of mammals
Describe the arrangement of teeth in the jaw bones of herbivores, carnivores and of humans
State the importance of dental care in humans

subtopics.name: Feeding in protozoa and mammals
objectives: Describe feeding habits in protozoa and mammals

topics.name: Ecosystem
topics.content: Examples and explanation are required. Importance of ecological factors common to all habitats should be mentioned, and the importance of ecological factors to populations of animals and plants should be stressed.

subtopics.name: Ecological components
objectives: Define environment, biosphere, habitat, population, biotic community and ecosystem, with examples

subtopics.name: Components of the ecosystem
objectives: Distinguish biotic and abiotic components of the ecosystem

subtopics.name: Ecological factors
objectives: Describe ecological factors in aquatic and terrestrial ecosystems

subtopics.name: Simple measurement of ecological factors
objectives: Measure physical factors (climatic, topographic and gaseous), including humidity, temperature, wind speed, rainfall and light intensity
Describe edaphic factors: chemical and physical composition, moisture content and soil texture

topics.name: Food Webs and Trophic Levels
objectives: Classify organisms as producers (autotrophs), consumers (heterotrophs) and decomposers, including aquatic and terrestrial examples
Illustrate food relationships in a food chain and food web using specific examples
Describe the food/energy relationship in aquatic and terrestrial environments and the non-cyclic nature of energy transfer
Construct and explain pyramid of energy and pyramid of numbers and state the major differences between them
Describe decomposition in nature: micro and macro-decomposers, gaseous products and the role of decomposers
Observe demonstrations showing that carbon dioxide, hydrogen sulphide and heat energy are released during decomposition

subtopics.name: Biological associations
objectives: Describe the types of association: parasitism, symbiosis, commensalism and saprophytism, with named examples and their features of biological importance

subtopics.name: Adaptation of organisms to habitats
objectives: Describe adaptations of plants and animals to environmental conditions, with reference to differences in habitats

subtopics.name: Pollution of the atmosphere
objectives: Name the sources and effects of air pollutants: carbon monoxide, sulphur dioxide, oxides of nitrogen, smoke, smog, dust and particles from factories
Emphasize health hazards and damage to the environment
Mention the harmful effects of noise from generators, aeroplanes and electronic sound gadgets

subtopics.name: Water and soil pollution
objectives: State the types and effects of water and soil pollutants: detergents, insecticides, artificial fertilizers, herbicides, sewage, domestic and industrial wastes, crude oil and decaying organic matter
Mention the health hazards and harmful effects on organisms, including oil spillage

subtopics.name: Ecological succession
objectives: Describe structural changes in species composition, variety or diversity and increase in numbers
State the general characteristics and outcomes of succession
Study succession in an abandoned farmland, lawn and pond to discover the sequence of colonization by plants

subtopics.name: Primary succession
objectives: Describe succession in terrestrial and aquatic habitats

subtopics.name: Secondary succession and climax
objectives: Describe secondary succession and the climax as the characteristic of a stable ecosystem

subtopics.name: Factors that affect population size
objectives: Explain the effects of natality, mortality, emigration, immigration, food shortage, predation, competition and diseases on population size

subtopics.name: Preservation and storage of foods
objectives: Describe methods of preserving and storing food, including the use of ionizing radiations
Explain the biological basis of preserving and storing food
Mention local methods such as drying, salting and smoking

subtopics.name: The life of selected insects
objectives: Describe the external features, mode of life, adaptation to habitat and economic importance of weevils and cotton strainers

subtopics.name: Control of pests
objectives: Describe physical, chemical and biological methods of pest control and state their advantages and disadvantages

subtopics.name: Carriers of microorganisms
objectives: Mention the effects of microorganisms on our bodies
Name carriers of microorganisms: housefly, mosquitoes and tsetsefly

subtopics.name: Microorganisms in action
objectives: Describe beneficial effects of microorganisms in nature, medicine and industries
Perform experiments on fermentation and curdling of milk to illustrate beneficial uses
Describe harmful effects and diseases caused by microorganisms: cholera, measles, malaria and ring worm, with causative organisms, mode of transmission and symptoms

subtopics.name: Towards better health
objectives: Describe methods of controlling harmful microorganisms: high temperature, antibiotics, antiseptics, high salinity and dehydration, and their effects
Describe ways of controlling vectors, including the housefly and mosquito

subtopics.name: Public health
objectives: Explain the importance of refuse and sewage disposal in maintaining good health practices
Explain the terms immunization, vaccination and inoculation and show how they are related
Mention the various forms of immunization

topics.name: Conservation of Natural Resources
objectives: Identify the resources to be conserved: soil, water, wildlife, forest and minerals
Explain the meaning and need for conservation of natural resources
Mention problems of conservation in relation to economic and social development, overgrazing and poaching
Describe ways of ensuring conservation: agencies responsible, conservation education, conservation laws and benefits of conservation

topics.name: Variation in Population
topics.content: Variation can be classified into morphological and physiological or continuous and discontinuous.

subtopics.name: Morphological variations
objectives: Describe morphological variations in size, height and weight, colour (skin, eye, hair, coat of animals) and finger prints
Measure heights and weights of pupils of the same age group and plot graphs of frequency distribution
Observe and record skin colour, colour pattern of animals (cow, goat, rabbit) and plants (maize cob and leaves)
Make finger prints and classify them into arches, loops, whorls and compounds

subtopics.name: Physiological variations
objectives: Describe physiological variations: ability to roll tongue, ability to taste phenylthiocarbamide (PTC) and blood groups (ABO classification)

subtopics.name: Genetic terminologies
objectives: Define gene, genotype, phenotype, dominant, recessive, allele, locus, test cross and back cross

subtopics.name: Transmission and expression of characteristics
objectives: Describe hereditary variation with reference to transmissible characters such as colour of skin, eye, hair, blood group, sickle cell, shape of face and nose
Describe Mendel's experiments (red and white flowered peas), including monohybrid and dihybrid inheritance
Describe Mendelian traits and Mendelian laws

subtopics.name: Chromosomes: the basis of heredity
objectives: Describe the structure of chromosomes, observing chromosomes in prepared slides of cells and root tips of onion or lily
Study the structure of DNA and gene replication using models and charts
Explain the transmission of hereditary characters from parents to offspring using segregation of genes at meiosis and recombination at fertilization

subtopics.name: Probability in genetics
objectives: Describe hybrid formation (computation of probability is not required)

subtopics.name: Linkage, sex determination and sex-linked characters
objectives: Explain the terms linkage, sex determination and sex-linked characters such as haemophilia, colour blindness, baldness and hairy ear lobes

subtopics.name: Application of heredity in agriculture
objectives: Study data on cross-breeding experiments
Give examples of new varieties of crops and livestock obtained through cross-breeding
Explain advantages and disadvantages of cross-fertilization, out-breeding and inbreeding

subtopics.name: Application of heredity in medicine
objectives: Mention the application of heredity in marriage counselling, with reference to sickle cell anaemia and rhesus factor

topics.name: Behavioural Adaptations in Social Animals
objectives: Describe the behavioural adaptations of termites and bees
Identify the various castes of social insects and the division of labour and roles of different castes
Give examples of communication among animals such as contact notes and warning cries
Make reference to basking by lizard, territorial behaviour in birds and lizards, and hibernation and aestivation under unfavourable conditions
Mention the behaviour of an organism as a member of a group and the effect of grouping on behaviour

topics.name: Evolution
topics.content: Candidates are expected to know the evolutionary trends in plants and animals such as from simple to complex structural adaptations and from aquatic to terrestrial organisms. The role of mutation in evolution should be mentioned.

subtopics.name: Evidence of evolution
objectives: Mention evidence of evolution: paleontology (fossil records), comparative biochemistry, geographical distribution, comparative anatomy and physiology, adaptive radiation, comparative embryology and systematics

subtopics.name: Theories of evolution
objectives: Mention the contributions of Lamarck and Darwin to the development of the theory of evolution

topics.name: Cell Theory
objectives: Outline the cell theory including the work of Hooke, Dujardin, Schleiden and Schwann

topics.name: Irritability as a Basic Characteristic of Protoplasm
objectives: Describe the types of responses: taxis and nastism
State environmental factors that evoke responses, e.g. temperature and pH

topics.name: Diseases of the Excretory Organs
objectives: Describe diseases of the kidney (nephritis, kidney stone and diuresis), their effects and remedies
Describe diseases of the liver (infective hepatitis, cancer of the liver and gall stones), their effects and remedies
Mention the excretory organs of earthworm and insects

topics.name: Sense Organs: Nose, Tongue and Skin
topics.content: The process of perception of smell, including the roles of sensory cells in the nose and olfactory lobes, should be studied. Experiments should be carried out to determine the different areas of the tongue associated with different tastes. The association between the organs of taste and smell should be mentioned, with mention of taste buds. The function of the skin as a sensory organ should be emphasized.

subtopics.name: Nose
objectives: Describe the process of perception of smell

subtopics.name: Tongue
objectives: Determine by experiment the areas of the tongue associated with different tastes
Mention the association between the organs of taste and smell

subtopics.name: Skin (sense organ)
objectives: Describe the function of the skin as a sensory organ

topics.name: Reproduction and Development in Animals and Seed Germination

subtopics.name: Courtship behaviour in animals

subtopics.name: Metamorphosis and life history of housefly

subtopics.name: Adaptive features in a developing animal
